title: Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi
summary: Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi, born Dyah Gitarja, was the third ruler of Majapahit and is dated to 1328–1350. One source says she took the throne after Jayanagara was murdered in 1328, her mother Gayatri Rajapatni appointing her queen, and that the kingdom grew much larger under her. She ruled until her mother's death in 1350, when her son Hayam Wuruk succeeded her.

uncertainty.note: Ancient Origins and Facts and Details both give 1328-1350 for the reign. Her birth and death dates are not given on the opened pages. Other accounts give 1329 for accession; that was not on an opened page.

where.modern_name: Trowulan, Mojokerto Regency, East Java, Indonesia (pinned to Majapahit's capital region; the location of Tribhuwana's own palace in the Kahuripan area, around Jombang, is still an open question per the Jakarta Post)
where.historical_name: Majapahit, East Java: capital at Trowulan; Tribhuwana ruled as queen and earlier held Kahuripan

importance.justification: Sources identify her as Majapahit's third ruler and its strongest female ruler, whose reign is followed by the era the Jakarta Post calls its golden age.

reviewer_note: Reign dates come from two popular sites that may share an origin; the only non-"other" source is the Jakarta Post, which gives no dates. The Gajah Mada link and the 1331 rebellion are not stated here since they were not on a source that supports them. Pin is the Majapahit capital, with a wide radius, because her own seat is unconfirmed. Withdrawn from the globe: sources are a newspaper and popular sites only; needs a museum, university or government source.
